question: Does adding crossed initial-state/tilt-history training data improve unseen initial-group predictions, especially reverse tilt history, without regressing old groups?
initialization: fresh zero-output ResidualMLP; do not warm start baseline

pairs.weighting: equal initial groups, snapshots per group, axis/amplitude rows per snapshot

normalization: retained_training_v2, all retained S2 and paired training inputs; fixed SI loss and residual gains
selection: fixed final update only; no development-validation checkpoint selection
evaluation: Same frozen baseline and final candidate on all old/new development groups, amplitudes and both new histories.
Separate SI state RMSE, strong response direction/cosine/magnitude, and noise-unresolved counts.
S2 complete-route validation H8 position protection.

Record per-group/amp H32 position <=1.1x baseline, no reduction of strong positive or cosine>=0.5 counts; S2 route H8 position <=1.1x baseline. These are regression diagnostics, not control admission.
stop_conditions: data/source hash or split identity mismatch
